Thank you very much!

However, I would like to remind you of some things to pay attention to when fixing this bug. This bug is related to the fact that *SkeletonModificationStack2D* is designed as a *Resource* type. According to the implementation principles of the underlying *API*, the relationship between *Skeleton2D and SkeletonModificationStack2D* should be one-to-one. This relationship is established through the exposed methods, namely *Skeleton2D.get_modification_stack* and *SkeletonModificationStack2D.get_skeleton*, whose return values are always a single object rather than multiple objects.

Strangely enough, *SkeletonModificationStack2D* is designed as a resource rather than a node, so by design it should be shareable, allowing multiple *Skeleton2D* nodes to share a single modification stack, meaning a many-to-one relationship.This inevitably leads to a problem: if two skeleton scene instances both point to the same modification stack, but this modification stack only points back to one of these skeleton scene instances, then one of the skeletons will indirectly call upon the other skeleton through the modification stack. This is not allowed, and as a result, the console will continuously display error messages in red, such as the following:

```bash
ERROR: Drawing is only allowed inside this node's `_draw()`, functions connected to its `draw` signal, or when it receives NOTIFICATION_DRAW.
```

In fact, this issue clearly has a more developer-friendly way to be improved, and the specific implementation wouldn't be very difficult. For example:
 
- Since *Skeleton2D* and *SkeletonModificationStack2D* are logically always in a one-to-one correspondence, we could find a way to set the default value of the *resource_local_to_scene* property of the *SkeletonModificationStack2D* resource to true, ensuring that this exception does not occur under default settings.
 
- Additionally, if we could detect this situation in the code logic, we could implement a more user-friendly, foolproof error message, such as "You should always set the resource_local_to_scene property of SkeletonModificationStack2D to true" to alert developers.
 
- Moreover, as the author of [this issue](https://app4.secure.forcepoint.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10247) pointed out, under this one-to-one design architecture, it is inherently unreasonable for *SkeletonModificationStack2D* to be designed as a resource. Therefore, the most sensible approach would be to refactor it into a new node inheriting from Node2D, which would fundamentally and completely solve this problem.

Unfortunately, since this issue was first raised in [4.0-rc3](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/73888), in [4.0.2](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/76849), in [4.1.1](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/81433) and [4.1.1.stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/79960), in [4.2.1.stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86945), in [4.3.stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/97651), in [4.4.beta1](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102054) and [4.4.beta2](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102541), and up to the recent [4.6.1.stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/117090), we still haven't seen any changes regarding this matter. We only see issues that remain open, along with various strange error logs.

Judging from [this issue](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/65265), this *SkeletonModificationStack2D* is like a Cthulhu-esque ancient god in the realm of 2D skeletons—something that cannot be looked upon directly, nor understood. Once you attempt to summon its presence across multiple instances, you will fall into the endless abyss of frantic errors. Developers can only grope in the darkness (referring to the latest UI of 4.6.1), using incantations like *resource_local_to_scene = true* to temporarily appease this slumbering leviathan, praying that it doesn't go berserk again in the next version update. And that *Godot* leadership team, renowned for its open-source spirit, seems currently incapable of taming this voracious monster. They are busy developing other, more dazzling features, neglecting this ancient curse buried deep within the 2D skeleton system. Now, we warriors known as developers must continue to coexist with these indescribable errors, experiencing in every red sea of *ERROR: Drawing is only allowed...* the pure terror of facing the unknown, just as Lovecraft described.

Sigh, waiting for Godot. Waiting for better Godot. (To be continued...)

Thank you so much for your in depth description.
I'll do my best to put to sleep this tormenting beast once and for all.
Again, thank for this feedback, I'll update here once I have progress in this matter.
